source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Bronchiolitis, commonly caused by RSV in young children, rather than the teething discomfort the family member is currently assuming explains this presentation","B":"Simple teething discomfort with no respiratory involvement, similar to what the family member is currently assuming about this infant's symptoms","C":"A normal cold requiring no further clinical evaluation, contrary to what this particular combination of respiratory findings actually warrants","D":"An unrelated cardiac condition requiring cardiology referral, which would not explain the preceding respiratory illness and current findings together"}}
source_row.rationale: Wheezing, tachypnea, nasal congestion, and increased work of breathing following a preceding viral upper respiratory illness are classic findings of bronchiolitis, most commonly caused by RSV, primarily affecting infants and young children under 2 years old, and requiring supportive care with close monitoring of respiratory status, particularly in higher-risk infants.
source_row.source_name: American Academy of Pediatrics — Bronchiolitis Clinical Practice Guideline
source_row.stem: An infant presents with wheezing, tachypnea, nasal congestion, and increased work of breathing following a preceding upper respiratory illness, and a family member assumes this is probably just new teething discomfort making the baby breathe a bit differently.
